title: Comparative Veterinary Anatomy & Physiology For The Veterinary Technician
description: Comparative anatomy and physiology for veterinary technicians. Clinically relevant anatomy and physiology of the major domestic animals and birds, and includes a discussion of the similarities and differences among the species. Emphasis is placed on the normal structure and function of the major organ systems as the foundation for understanding pathology and pathophysiology of disease. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Know and explain the normal physiology of selected organs and organ systems of domestic animals and relate it to the clinical practice of veterinary technology.
Recognize and identify the normal anatomy of selected organs and organ systems of domestic animals and relate it to the clinical practice of veterinary technology.
objectives: Analyze and evaluate the relationship between GI system structure and function, and describe clinical applications of the GI system in various domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between nervous system structure and function, and describe clinical applications of the nervous system in various domestic species
Describe the structure and function of the special senses, and describe clinical applications of the special senses in various domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between endocrine system structure and function, and describe clinical applications of the endocrine system in various domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between urinary system structure and function, and describe clinical applications of the urinary system in various domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between reproductive system structure and function, and describe clinical applications of the reproductive system in various domestic species
Compare avian to mammalian anatomy and physiology, and apply to the clinical setting
content: Application of GI system in clinical practice
Application of neurology in clinical practice
Application of special senses in clinical practice
Application of the endocrine system to clinical practice
The urinary tract in clinical practice
Application of the reproductive system in clinical practice
Basic orientation to the anatomy and physiology of avian species and comparison to mammals
lab: Cell and tissue identification for these systems:
Identification of major cell and tissue types on prepared histology slides of systems covered
Participate in a necropsy procedure as an essential skill to apply anatomical knowledge
Comparative anatomy between mammalian and avian structures
